### 1. Polymathic AI and Princeton Researchers Release FlashMap, a Flow Map Drafter for 6.14x Faster LLM Decoding

**Source:** MarkTechPost  
**Link:** [https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/10/28/flashmap-flow-map-speculative-decoding/](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/10/28/flashmap-flow-map-speculative-decoding/)

HEADLINE: Princeton and Polymathic AI Unveil FlashMap: A Revolutionary Tool for Accelerated LLM Decoding

SUMMARY: Researchers from Polymathic AI, Princeton University, and USC ISI have introduced FlashMap, a novel flow map drafter that enhances large language model (LLM) decoding speeds significantly. By drafting 16 tokens simultaneously in a single pass, FlashMap achieves up to 6.14 times faster lossless decoding for the Qwen3-8B model.

KEY POINTS:
- FlashMap allows for joint drafting of 16 tokens in one decoding pass.
- It demonstrates a speedup of up to 6.14 times compared to traditional methods on the Qwen3-8B model.
- The tool is a collaboration between researchers from Polymathic AI, Princeton University, and USC ISI.
- This advancement could lead to more efficient LLM applications in various domains.

IMPACT: The introduction of FlashMap represents a significant leap in LLM processing speed, which could enhance real-time applications and broaden the usability of AI language models across industries.

### 3. Meet LEANN: An Open-Source Vector Index that Shrinks a 60M-Chunk RAG Index from 201 GB to 6 GB

**Source:** MarkTechPost  
**Link:** [https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/10/27/leann-vector-index-mlsys-2026/](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/10/27/leann-vector-index-mlsys-2026/)

HEADLINE: LEANN: Revolutionary Open-Source Vector Index Cuts RAG Index Size from 201 GB to 6 GB

SUMMARY: Researchers at UC Berkeley have introduced LEANN, an open-source vector index that dramatically reduces the size of a 60 million-chunk RAG index from 201 GB to just 6 GB. By employing a pruned graph and recomputing embeddings during query time, LEANN achieves 90% recall with HNSW accuracy, though it sacrifices some search speed.

KEY POINTS:
- LEANN reduces the memory footprint of large vector indices significantly.
- It operates at 90% recall accuracy using only 4 GB of memory compared to 188 GB.
- The method involves a pruned graph and requires recomputing embeddings at query time.
- While search speed may be slower (in seconds), it offers a more efficient storage solution for large datasets.

IMPACT: LEANN's development offers a game-changing solution for developers and businesses seeking to optimize memory usage in AI applications, particularly those dealing with large datasets in machine learning and data retrieval tasks.
